recentItems.title: Nepal's fight to rebuild after flood disaster | 101 East Documentary
recentItems.description:
On the morning of August 26, 2026, a devastating flash flood of rock and ice thundered from a high Himalayan mountain through Nepal's valleys, sweeping away homes, villages and bridges.

At least 1,400 people were killed and more than 5,000 people remain missing.

It was the latest in a series of natural disasters that have battered Nepal in recent years as climate change accelerates.

This programme follows the rescuers risking their lives to search for the missing and those providing aid and refuge for traumatised children and families.

101 East reveals Nepal's efforts to save lives and rebuild communities after a deadly natural disaster.

recentItems.title: Paraguay swears in Pedro Alliana after Santiago Pena impeachment
recentItems.description:
Paraguay has sworn in a new president after Santiago Pena was impeached and placed under house arrest. Celebrations followed outside Congress.

The Senate voted to impeach Pena for failing to carry out his presidential responsibilities, after the Prosecutor for Economic and Corruption Crimes ordered that he be put under house arrest. Pena is allegedly embroiled in a financial scandal that led to the collapse of the country’s largest online bank, Ueno Bank, this week, leaving millions of depositors unable to access their savings.

Also arrested was Carlos Carvallo, Central Bank president until he was forced to resign. He allegedly covered up serious financial irregularities at Ueno Bank, among other accusations.

His replacement, former vice president Pedro Alliana, was sworn in quickly. He vowed to govern for the most disadvantaged and said citizens affected by the financial crisis “will be fully compensated”. Millions fear losing their savings.

Al Jazeera’s Lucia Newman reports.

recentItems.title: Stephen Miller as Trump chief of staff means more executive action: Analysis
recentItems.description:
US President Donald Trump has named Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles, days after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections. Miller, a key architect of Trump’s hardline immigration policies, takes over on Monday.

Al Jazeera’s Alan Fisher says Miller is seen as loyal and able to enforce the president’s will. He says Wiles handed in her resignation in the Oval Office on Thursday night and is moving to the Trump political operation. Fisher says Miller will use all the levers of government to pursue Trump’s agenda, suggesting Trump working with Democrats is unlikely.

David Cohen, professor of political science and director of the Applied Politics Program at the University of Akron, says it depends on what the president wants, and that Trump is spoiling for a fight with Democrats. He says Wiles was a strong administrator, while Miller will focus on advising and enforcing, and expects more executive action, which may end up in the courts. Cohen says there is very little US support for the Iran war.
